seo.title: Audit Engagement Checklist for Smart Contract Auditors
seo.description: Complete smart contract audit methodology from scoping to report delivery. 75+ items covering security reviews used by professional audit firms.

content.intro: A complete audit methodology checklist covering every phase of a professional smart contract security review—from initial scoping to final report delivery. Used by top audit firms.

sections.heading: Pre-Engagement Phase
sections.description: Initial scoping and preparation before the audit begins.

items.title: Define audit scope and deliverables
items.description: Document all contracts in scope, lines of code, and expected deliverables. Clarify what's out of scope.

items.title: Gather project documentation
items.description: Collect whitepapers, architecture docs, previous audits, and design specifications from the client.

items.title: Identify external dependencies
items.description: List all oracles, external protocols, and third-party contracts the system interacts with.

items.title: Establish communication channels
items.description: Set up secure channels for questions, findings disclosure, and progress updates.

items.title: Review previous audit reports
items.description: Study any prior audits to understand historical issues and verify fixes.

items.title: Set up development environment
items.description: Clone repo, install dependencies, ensure all tests pass, set up debugging tools.

items.title: Identify key invariants with team
items.description: Discuss critical properties that must always hold—these become primary audit targets.

items.title: Map trust assumptions
items.description: Document what roles are trusted, what external systems are trusted, and failure assumptions.

sections.heading: Architecture Review
sections.description: High-level analysis of system design and threat model.

items.title: Map contract inheritance hierarchy
items.description: Diagram inheritance relationships and identify diamond/multiple inheritance issues.

items.title: Analyze access control model
items.description: Document all privileged roles, their capabilities, and how permissions can change.

items.title: Review upgrade mechanisms
items.description: Analyze proxy patterns, upgrade timelock, and storage collision risks.

items.title: Map external call graph
items.description: Document all cross-contract calls and potential reentrancy entry points.

items.title: Analyze economic model
items.description: Understand token flows, fee mechanisms, and economic invariants.

items.title: Review oracle integration design
items.description: Analyze price feed sources, staleness handling, and manipulation resistance.

items.title: Document state machine transitions
items.description: Map all possible states and valid transitions for stateful contracts.

items.title: Identify centralization risks
items.description: Document admin keys, multisig requirements, and potential single points of failure.

items.title: Review all external/public functions
items.description: Analyze each entry point for input validation, access control, and state changes.

items.title: Trace ETH and token flows
items.description: Follow all value transfers to verify accounting accuracy and prevent fund loss.

items.title: Analyze arithmetic operations
items.description: Check for overflow/underflow, rounding errors, and precision loss.

items.title: Review loop bounds and gas limits
items.description: Identify unbounded loops that could cause DoS via gas exhaustion.

items.title: Check reentrancy guards
items.description: Verify CEI pattern or reentrancy locks on all external calls.

items.title: Analyze storage layouts
items.description: Check for slot collisions in upgradeable contracts and packed struct issues.

items.title: Review error handling
items.description: Verify appropriate use of require/revert, custom errors, and error messages.

items.title: Check event emissions
items.description: Verify all state changes emit appropriate events for off-chain tracking.

items.title: Run static analyzers (Slither, Mythril)
items.description: Execute static analysis tools and triage all findings.

items.title: Execute symbolic execution (Manticore)
items.description: Use symbolic execution to explore edge cases and constraint violations.

items.title: Run fuzzing campaigns
items.description: Set up Echidna or Foundry fuzzing with property-based tests.

items.title: Perform formal verification checks
items.description: Use Certora or Halmos for critical invariant verification.

items.title: Analyze gas optimization opportunities
items.description: Identify expensive operations and suggest optimizations.

items.title: Check code coverage
items.description: Ensure test suite covers all branches and edge cases.

items.title: Run dependency audit
items.description: Check imported libraries for known vulnerabilities.

items.title: Verify compiler settings
items.description: Check Solidity version, optimizer settings, and via-IR usage.

items.title: Test flash loan attack vectors
items.description: Attempt price manipulation, governance attacks, and liquidity drainage via flash loans.

items.title: Analyze oracle manipulation resistance
items.description: Test TWAP effectiveness, multi-oracle fallbacks, and manipulation costs.

items.title: Check MEV extraction risks
items.description: Identify sandwich attack vectors, frontrunning opportunities, and backrunning risks.

items.title: Test liquidation mechanics
items.description: Verify liquidation thresholds, incentives, and cascade prevention.

items.title: Analyze interest rate models
items.description: Test utilization curves, rate jumps, and economic stability.

items.title: Check slippage protections
items.description: Verify deadline parameters, minimum output amounts, and price bounds.

items.title: Test deposit/withdrawal edge cases
items.description: Check first depositor attacks, rounding exploits, and share inflation.

items.title: Analyze governance attack vectors
items.description: Test vote buying, flash loan voting, and proposal spam attacks.

sections.heading: Integration Testing
sections.description: Testing contract interactions with external systems.

items.title: Test mainnet fork scenarios
items.description: Run integration tests against forked mainnet state with real protocol data.

items.title: Verify cross-chain bridge interactions
items.description: Test message passing, finality assumptions, and bridge failure handling.

items.title: Test oracle failure scenarios
items.description: Simulate stale prices, oracle downtime, and manipulation attempts.

items.title: Verify upgrade path correctness
items.description: Test storage migrations, initialization, and rollback scenarios.

items.title: Test emergency procedures
items.description: Verify pause mechanisms, emergency withdrawals, and circuit breakers.

items.title: Analyze composability risks
items.description: Test interactions with other DeFi protocols and potential conflicts.

items.title: Test gas under network congestion
items.description: Verify critical functions work within block gas limits during high gas periods.

items.title: Verify off-chain component integration
items.description: Test keeper bots, relayers, and off-chain computation correctness.

items.title: Classify severity accurately
items.description: Use consistent severity ratings: Critical, High, Medium, Low, Informational.

items.title: Write clear reproduction steps
items.description: Provide PoC code or step-by-step instructions to reproduce each finding.

items.title: Explain impact clearly
items.description: Describe worst-case scenarios, affected users, and potential fund loss.

items.title: Provide actionable recommendations
items.description: Suggest specific code changes or architectural improvements.

items.title: Link to relevant references
items.description: Reference similar past exploits, documentation, or security guidelines.

items.title: Track finding status
items.description: Maintain status tracking: Open, Acknowledged, Fixed, Won't Fix.

items.title: Document mitigating factors
items.description: Note any factors that reduce severity or exploitability.

items.title: Cross-reference related findings
items.description: Link findings that share root causes or have combined impact.

sections.heading: Report Delivery
sections.description: Finalizing and delivering the audit report.

items.title: Conduct internal peer review
items.description: Have findings reviewed by another auditor before client delivery.

items.title: Verify fix implementations
items.description: Review all fixes and confirm they address the root cause without introducing new issues.

items.title: Update finding statuses
items.description: Mark all findings as Fixed, Partially Fixed, Acknowledged, or Disputed.

items.title: Write executive summary
items.description: Summarize overall security posture, key risks, and recommendations.

items.title: Document audit limitations
items.description: Clearly state scope boundaries, time constraints, and what wasn't reviewed.

items.title: Provide deployment recommendations
items.description: Suggest monitoring, incident response, and post-deployment security measures.

items.title: Schedule final walkthrough
items.description: Review findings with client team and answer technical questions.

items.title: Archive audit materials
items.description: Securely store PoCs, notes, and tooling output for future reference.

proTips: Build a personal vulnerability checklist: Maintain your own list of patterns based on past audits and public exploits. Update it after every engagement.
Read the code multiple times with different lenses: First pass for understanding, second for logic errors, third for edge cases, fourth for economic attacks.
Always question trust assumptions: Admin keys get compromised, oracles fail, external protocols get hacked. Test what happens when trusted components misbehave.
Write PoCs for every medium+ finding: A working exploit removes all doubt about severity and helps clients prioritize fixes.
Study past exploits weekly: Follow rekt.news, DeFiHackLabs, and post-mortems. Most vulnerabilities are variations of known patterns.
content.conclusion: Master smart contract security and join the elite ranks of blockchain auditors.
